sentences.text:
Through: Mr.Sunil Kumar Gautam,
 State with SI Dine  R2/complainant in   CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGESH KHANNA  ORDER % 21.02.2023 1.

Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.58/2020 under Section 406/498A/509/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Nangloi, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 04.02.2016 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
On 11.04.2017 one male child Rohan was born who is in care and custody of respondent No.2.
However, due to matrimonial discord, the couple started living separately from each other and on the complaint of respondent No.2 aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
They have settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 19.05.2022 before the Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.
The parties have also obtained divorce by mutual consent.

Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 has agreed to pay Rs.3.00 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future, stridhan, and dowry articles etc.
The petitioner No.1 has already paid the settled amount of Rs.3.00 lacs to respondent No.2, which is not being disputed by the respondent No.2.
3. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

4. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the Arvind Kumar & Ors vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) Anr on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117418696/
1 FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.

sentences.text: In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
5. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.58/2020 under Section 406/498A/509/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Nangloi, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
The above settlement would not affect the lawful rights/claims of minor child, which may be exercised, in future, against the petitioner No.1.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
